Goldsmith
GOLD-smith
noun
From gold (Old English gold) and smith (Old English smiþ, a worker in metal); rendering Hebrew tsoreph, a refiner or founder — one who melts, refines, and overlays in gold.

Biblical Definition

A goldsmith refines the metal and works it: melting, casting, beating it thin, and overlaying wood or stone with plate. Scripture shows him in two opposite postures, and the contrast is the whole lesson. In Isaiah he is the idol-maker’s partner: “the workman melteth a graven image, and the goldsmith spreadeth it over with gold” (Isa 40:19); the carpenter cheers him on, and they nail the finished god down “that it should not be moved” (Isa 41:7) — a deity requiring carpentry to keep it upright. Isaiah drives it home elsewhere: men lavish gold out of the bag, “and hire a goldsmith; and he maketh it a god: they fall down, yea, they worship” (Isa 46:6). The prophet is not describing superstition among savages; he is describing an economy, a supply chain, a trade contracted to produce an object of worship. Then turn to Nehemiah. When the wall of Jerusalem lay in rubble, “next unto him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths” (Neh 3:8), and a goldsmith’s son took his own section too (Neh 3:31). Men whose hands were trained to fine, delicate, valuable work laid down the graver and picked up rubble to rebuild the city of God. Same trade, same skill, two masters. The goldsmith who serves an idol builds a god that must be fastened down; the goldsmith who serves the LORD helps rebuild a wall that stands.

Webster 1828 Definition

One who works in gold — refining, casting, and overlaying; in Scripture both idol-maker and wall-builder.

expand to see more

GOLDSMITH, one whose occupation is to manufacture vessels and ornaments of gold; a worker and refiner of gold.

From gold and smith; Hebrew tsoreph, a refiner or founder.

Isaiah repeatedly sets him at the idol-maker’s bench (Isa 40:19; Isa 41:7; Isa 46:6).

Nehemiah sets the goldsmiths on the broken wall of Jerusalem (Neh 3:8, 31).

The same skill serves a nailed-down idol or the city of God.

Key Scripture

Isa 40:19 — "The workman melteth a graven image, and the goldsmith spreadeth it over with gold, and casteth silver chains."

Isa 41:7 — "So the carpenter encouraged the goldsmith, and he that smootheth with the hammer him that smote the anvil, saying, It is ready for the sodering: and he fastened it with nails, that it should not be moved."

Isa 46:6 — "They lavish gold out of the bag, and weigh silver in the balance, and hire a goldsmith; and he maketh it a god: they fall down, yea, they worship."

Neh 3:8 — "Next unto him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths. Next unto him also repaired Hananiah the son of one of the apothecaries, and they fortified Jerusalem unto the broad wall."

Modern Corruption

A skill is never neutral: the same hands that gild an idol can rebuild a wall.

expand to see more

Isaiah’s irony is the sharpest treatment of idolatry in Scripture and it is aimed at a tradesman. A god is commissioned, costed, cast, gilded, and then nailed to the floor so it will not fall over. The prophet does not argue that the idol is powerless; he lets the manufacturing process argue it. And the modern reader should not congratulate himself on having outgrown the workshop. The idols of a gilded age are made in the same way — conceived by desire, financed out of the bag, fabricated by skilled professionals, and defended by everyone employed in their production. Whatever a man will spend himself to obtain, adorn, and prop upright is his god; the Second Commandment reaches the advertising studio as surely as the founder’s furnace.

The recovery is in Nehemiah 3. Uzziel of the goldsmiths, and Hananiah the son of one of the apothecaries, repaired the wall and fortified Jerusalem unto the broad wall. Neither man was a mason. Both left the fine bench for common labour because the city of God was in ruins and the work needed hands. That chapter is the sanest picture of vocation in the Old Testament: priests, perfumers, goldsmiths, merchants, and the daughters of Shallum, each with a named section, none of them despising the mortar. A man’s trade gives him tools and standing; it does not give him leave to sit down when the wall is broken.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

A refiner and worker of gold; in Isaiah he gilds idols, in Nehemiah he rebuilds the wall.

expand to see more

Goldsmith — gold + smith, a worker in metal.

Hebrew tsoreph means a refiner or founder, one who smelts and purifies.

He overlays the graven image with plate (Isa 40:19).

The finished god must be nailed down lest it topple (Isa 41:7).

Goldsmiths repaired their own section of Jerusalem’s wall (Neh 3:8, 31).

Usage

"They hire a goldsmith, and he maketh it a god — idolatry as an industry."

"A god that must be fastened with nails cannot fasten anything else."

"The goldsmiths of Nehemiah 3 laid down the graver and took up the wall."
